name: Hotel Saravana Bhavan
signature_dish: South Indian meals and tiffin — masala dosa, mini tiffin, filter coffee
why_it_matters: This Gandhi Road branch, opened in 1995, is the oldest Saravana Bhavan outlet in Kanchipuram and the most reliable air-conditioned vegetarian meal in a temple town with otherwise modest dining. Central location near the silk-saree shops and a short ride from the major temples makes it the default clean stop for travellers between darshans.
insider_tip: Order the rava dosa or the South Indian thali; ask whether the kitchen has Kanchipuram-style spiced idli that day. Has parking — useful in the congested Gandhi Road belt. Busy at lunch with both pilgrims and saree shoppers. Cash + cards + UPI.

name: The Dakshin (GRT Regency Kanchipuram)
signature_dish: Multi-cuisine vegetarian buffet with North Indian and Chinese dishes
why_it_matters: The restaurant at GRT Regency on Gandhi Road, consistently ranked Kanchipuram's top dining address on TripAdvisor — its expansive vegetarian buffet at a reasonable price, pleasant air-conditioned ambience and attentive service make it the comfort option in a town where most eateries are basic tiffin halls.
insider_tip: The buffet is the value play, especially at lunch. Cleanest, most comfortable air-conditioned dining in town if you want a break from temple-town basic. Hotel parking. Cash + cards.

name: Adyar Ananda Bhavan (A2B)
signature_dish: South Indian tiffin and sweets — dosa, idli, mysore pak, jangri
why_it_matters: The Kanchipuram outlet of Adyar Ananda Bhavan (A2B), the Tamil Nadu vegetarian restaurant and sweet chain with 145+ outlets — located near the bus stand on Nellukara Street, it pairs reliable tiffin with a strong sweet counter, handy for picking up mysore pak and jangri to take home alongside a quick meal.
insider_tip: Eat the tiffin, then buy sweets at the counter — A2B's mysore pak and jangri travel well as gifts. Near the bus stand, so convenient when arriving or leaving. Open 7am-11pm. Cash + cards + UPI.
signature_address: 68B Nellukara Street, near bus stand, Little Kanchipuram, Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu 631501

name: Sangeetha Vegetarian Restaurant
signature_dish: South Indian tiffin and meals — idli, dosa, vada, thali
why_it_matters: A dependable pure-vegetarian restaurant on Nellukara Street serving the standard South and North Indian tiffin-and-meals spread — one of the better-rated everyday eateries in central Kanchipuram, open 7am to 11pm and handy for travellers needing a clean, quick meal between temple visits and saree shopping.
insider_tip: The mini tiffin is the efficient order; lunch thali if you want a full meal. Open early for breakfast before the temples get busy. Cash + UPI.

name: Varadaraja Perumal Temple Kovil Idli (Madappalli)
signature_dish: Kanchipuram kovil idli — the foot-long spiced idli offered as temple prasadam
why_it_matters: Kanchipuram idli — the foot-long idli spiced with pepper, cumin, ginger, cashew and curry leaves and steamed in dried mandharai leaves — originated as naivedyam offered to Lord Varadaraja. Multiple food writers confirm the truest version is still made only in the temple kitchen (madappalli) of the Varadaraja Perumal Temple and distributed as prasadam; restaurants only approximate it.
insider_tip: This is prasadam, not a restaurant — availability follows temple ritual timings, so ask at the madappalli counter during the morning or midday offering hours. The leaf-steamed temple version is distinctly more fragrant than any restaurant copy. Small cash only.
signature_address: Varadaraja Perumal Temple, Little Kanchipuram, Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu 631501
